Maria L.: Quick help pls — customer sent a request_id 9f2b1c, I can see a trace in Jaeger but the Redwood Console trace view shows no logs. Where do folks normally jump to?

Devin K.: Two routes I use: Console -> Observability -> Traces -> open trace -> 'Show related logs' (expands time + filters). Or CLI quick query: `redwood logs query --filter \"request_id:9f2b1c OR req_id:9f2b1c\" --env=prod --since 2h`

Maria L.: I don't see any 'Show related logs' button on that trace page when opened from an alert. UI maybe different from the list view.

Logan (oncall): Yeah, alerts link opens the trace in a compact view without some controls. If you open the same trace from Traces list it shows the full action bar. Also check the time window on the trace — the related logs filter uses span start/end. Expand to +/- 1m to be safe.

Maria L.: Got it. Also our gateway logs `req_id` instead of `request_id`. That explains why the console linkage missed them.

Jess - infra: For mapping trace->log keys I usually run: `redwood traces export --id 9a8b-xyz --format json | jq -r '.spans[].attributes | to_entries[] | select(.key|test("req|request")) | .key +":"+.value'` then feed those into logs query. If you only have a trace id, that gets you the canonical key names.

Devin K.: Note on sampling/archiving: traces can be sampled but logs may have been moved to cold indexes. If you suspect that, use `--archived` with the logs CLI: `redwood logs query --filter \"req_id:9f2b1c\" --archived --env prod` (hits the cold store).

Logan (oncall): Permissions check too — `logs.read` on prod is required. If CLI returns 403, ping Security for a short-lived role.

Maria L.: Tried the export+jq trick and found `req_id:9f2b1c`. Ran `redwood logs query --filter \"req_id:9f2b1c\" --service gateway --since 30m` and pulled the 502 in front of the auth service. There was a downstream trace id `9a8b-xyz`.

Jess - infra: If anyone wants a reusable one-liner to go trace->logs:
```
redwood traces export --id 9a8b-xyz --format json \
  | jq -r '.spans[].attributes | to_entries[] | select(.key|test("req|request")) | .value' \
  | sort -u \
  | xargs -I{} redwood logs query --filter \"req_id:{} OR request_id:{}\" --since 1h
```

Devin K.: I'll add a console bookmark that opens traces with the expanded time range + related logs filter and share it with the team. Saves a bunch of hunting.

Maria L.: Awesome. One small UX bug to note: when opening a trace from the Alerts detail page the 'Show related logs' action is missing. Can someone file a ticket?

Logan (oncall): Filed INFRA-8732 for the missing action path and CC'd @dev-ux.

Ops-bot: log-shipper status: all pipelines healthy, no lag > 45s (04:21 UTC)

Maria L.: Thanks all, I have what I need. Will post a short follow-up in #incidents if we need a postmortem. :thumbsup:
